EduBrisk at Sharjah Indian School, Boys this year

What you are looking at

This page is built from the platform’s record of every test a student attempted this academic year, with the mark and date of each try, set against the school’s class lists, its EduBrisk usage report and its own internal marks in iAspire. Grade 12 has no attempts this year and is shown, on its own, from last year’s record. Nothing here is estimated — each figure counts actual rows in those records.

The charts below read across all grades at once. Pick a grade from the filter above and they step aside for that grade’s own subject, chapter and test tables.

Click any student in the engagement chart to open their record — attempts, time per test, average mark and every subject mark. Hovering any point or row shows its exact figures.

Summary

Where this comes from
The platform’s test-attempt export for Grades 3 to 10, counting attempts made from 1 April 2026. The roll for Grades 3 to 8 is the school’s EduBrisk student login lists for 2026–27; for Grades 9 and 10 it is the student accounts in the school’s EduBrisk usage report. Grade 12 is shown from its 2025–26 attempts, made in Grade 11, against the students in that export.
What it shows
How many of the students on roll in the current selection have attempted at least one test, and how those attempts divide between a first try and later ones.
What it does not show
Whether a test was set as classwork or homework or taken voluntarily, and whether a student who did not attempt was absent or simply never opened the platform.
Who is not in it
Students who appear in iAspire but have no EduBrisk login — 74 of them across Grades 3 to 8. Twenty-seven names in the attempt exports (seven in Grades 3 to 8, twenty in Grades 9 and 10) could not be matched to a student on the roll; their attempts are listed under their section but not counted in any percentage. In Grades 3 to 10, attempts made in 2025–26 are left out. Section 10E has no attempt export.

These attempts come from another grade's file and are not counted in this grade's figures.

Evidence of impact

Across every grade. Click a grade on the chart to open it.

Where this comes from
The same attempt export. Only students who attempted the same test more than once feed this chart. The hours tile above it comes from the school’s EduBrisk usage report, added up over the students on roll; an account with no entry is counted as not recorded, not as zero. Grade 12, shown from 2025–26, is left out of every figure in this band.
What it shows
Where a second attempt took students — their mark on the first try against the best mark of their later tries.
What it does not show
Cause. A student who chooses to retake a test is usually one who means to do better, so this is the gain on retakes, not proof that the platform alone produced it.
Who is not in it
Students who attempted every test only once.

Engagement against attainment

Where this comes from
Across the bottom: the number of tests the student has attempted, from the platform export. Up the side: the student's average internal mark — the school's own assessment marks as held in iAspire, not EduBrisk marks.
What it shows
Whether the students putting in practice on the platform are also the students scoring well in school assessments.
What it does not show
Cause, in either direction. The dashed lines are the school’s fixed attainment bands — below 50% Below, 50–69% In line, 70% and over Above expectation — so they stay put when the grade or section changes. There is no fixed line for practice: read how much a student has practised off the bottom axis.
Who is not in it
The 234 students in Grades 3 to 8 with no internal mark in iAspire, and all of Grades 9, 10 and 12, which have no internal marks in this report. Students with no attempts are kept, in the lane on the left.

Class view

Where this comes from
One bubble per student in the selected section. Position is tests attempted against average internal mark from iAspire; colour is the student's average mark on EduBrisk tests. Size is the student’s time on the platform from the school’s EduBrisk usage report, ranked within the class rather than drawn to scale, so one very heavy user does not dwarf the rest.
What it shows
Four things about one class at once — who is practising, who is scoring in school, who is scoring on the platform, and who is spending time without it showing in either.
What it does not show
What the time was spent on — reading, practice or tests. An account with no entry in the usage report is shown as not recorded, not as zero. Colour is banded in fifteen-point steps.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark, so Grades 9, 10 and 12 have no class view. Students with no EduBrisk mark yet are shown in the palest colour and counted under the chart.

Subject-wise participation

Click a subject to see its tests.

Where this comes from
The attempt export, grouped by the subject each test belongs to.
What it shows
For each subject, how many students on roll have attempted at least one of its tests and how many have attempted none.
What it does not show
How well students did, and whether the chapters attempted match what the class has actually been taught so far.
Who is not in it
Subjects a grade has not been given on the platform — they do not appear at all.
SubjectChaptersTestsAttempted at least oneAttempted none

Section-wise participation

Where this comes from
The same export, grouped by the section each student sits in on the roll.
What it shows
Participation section by section for whatever subject or chapter is selected above.
What it does not show
It does not separate a section that was never set the work from one that was set it and did not do it.
Who is not in it
Students whose section is blank on the roll.

Achiever-level participation

Where this comes from
Achiever levels come from the school's internal assessment marks in iAspire. They are not derived from anything on EduBrisk.
What it shows
Whether participation differs between higher, middle and lower achievers.
What it does not show
Current standing. The level is fixed from the assessment it was taken from and does not move with platform results.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark on record carry no level, so they sit outside this table — they are still counted everywhere else.

Cross-test glance

Where this comes from
Every attempt on the tests in the selected chapter. A filled cell holds the best mark of that student's attempts.
What it shows
One row per student across all the tests in a chapter, so the gaps show up in a single view.
What it does not show
How many attempts produced the mark shown, or when it was taken.
Who is not in it
No one. Every student on roll in the selection has a row, whether they have taken anything or not.

Test-wise participation

Where this comes from
The attempt export, grouped by individual test.
What it shows
How many students attempted each test in the current selection, and how many did not.
What it does not show
Whether the test was assigned, and how long students were given.
Who is not in it
Tests nobody has attempted. The export is built from attempts, so a test with none does not appear.
